findings.title: Missing-input fallback reopens chunk ownership bypass on current batches
findings.trigger: Exchange the first valid A01/A02 rows, then delete or rename both input chunk files in the in-memory filesystem. Output rows and batch input remain unchanged.
findings.impact: Existence alone selects the legacy exception. A modern batch can disable ownership enforcement without changing its contract or batch number. agree consumes the accepted violating rows even with one remaining loader error.
findings.recommendation: Bind legacy exemption to explicit trusted batch/format metadata. Fail closed for required missing input chunks, and enforce equivalent ownership in all combination consumers.

findings.title: ID masking misses embedded tokens and parser exceptions
findings.trigger: Use an actual foreign item ID adjacent to an ASCII letter or underscore at the start of a repeated not_observable explanation. Separately put a foreign ID at the start of malformed JSON in another output chunk.
findings.impact: The rendered mine array is masked, but word boundaries miss IDs next to ASCII word characters. JSON.parse errors escape before that return and reveal foreign text to the single-chunk runner. The general no-foreign-ID output contract is therefore only partially fixed.
findings.recommendation: Redact known foreign IDs independent of ASCII word boundaries, and catch read/parse failures at the chunk output boundary with sanitized diagnostics. Preserve own IDs and explicitly define conservative masking of unknown ID-shaped strings.
